original_question: For a Krull monoid with finite class group, the Structure Theorem for Sets of Lengths says that there exist a nonnegative integer M and a finite nonempty set Delta* such that every set of lengths L(a) is an almost arithmetic multiprogression with bound M and difference d in Delta*. For the systems L(G) attached to finite abelian groups G, what is the rough order of magnitude of the smallest such bound as a function of the Davenport constant D(G)?
target_in_paper: Problem 6.24 in Section 6.4 (“The bound in the STSL”). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.08080))
correct_elements: Your draft already isolates the correct open problem: the asymptotic size of the STSL bound for the systems L(G) of finite abelian groups, measured in terms of the Davenport constant D(G). It also correctly connects the question to AAMP descriptions coming from the Structure Theorem for Sets of Lengths. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.08080))
missing_details: The paper is specifically about finite abelian groups G and the system L(G)=L(B(G)), where B(G) is the block monoid of zero-sum sequences over G; that identification is implicit in the draft. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.08080))

An AAMP in Definition 6.1 is determined not only by a bound M and a difference d but also by a shift y and a period D with {0,d}⊂D⊂[0,d], together with a decomposition L=y+(L'∪L*∪L''). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.08080))
In the STSL, the bound is universal for the whole system of sets of lengths of the monoid/group and does not depend on the individual element a. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.08080))

For the group-theoretic version, the nearby context singles out the natural choice of admissible differences as Δ*(G), not merely an arbitrary finite nonempty set Δ*. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.08080))

If one asks for the 'smallest such bound,' one should explicitly define M_G as the least universal bound for which every L∈L(G) is an AAMP with some difference d∈Δ*(G); Problem 6.24 itself speaks more informally of 'the bound in the STSL.' ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.08080))

To match the paper’s framing, it helps to record the current evidence: Theorem 6.22 gives an explicit upper bound of shape exp(c log D(G) · D(G)^2), while Example 6.23 shows that the dependence is at least quadratic in D(G). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.08080))

The interesting regime is asymptotic families with D(G) large; for very small groups the problem is trivial or nearly trivial, and Theorem 6.22 notes that the hypothesis D(G_P)≥3 excludes only the half-factorial cases. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.08080))
refined_question: For a finite abelian group G, let B(G) be the block monoid of zero-sum sequences over G and write L(G)=L(B(G)). Define M_G to be the smallest integer M≥0 such that every set L∈L(G) can be written in the almost arithmetic multiprogression form L=y+(L'∪L*∪L'')⊂y+D+dZ for some d∈Δ*(G), some period D with {0,d}⊂D⊂[0,d], some m≥0 with L*=[0,m]∩(D+dZ), and end pieces L'⊂[-M,-1], L''⊂m+[1,M]. What is the rough asymptotic order of M_G as a function of the Davenport constant D(G)? More specifically, between the explicit general upper bound supplied by Theorem 6.22 and the quadratic lower bound exhibited in Example 6.23, what is the true order of magnitude of the STSL bound for L(G) as D(G)→∞? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.08080))
justification: The draft is very close to the paper’s official wording. After introducing AAMPs in Definition 6.1 and the STSL in Theorem 6.3, the paper turns in Section 6.4 to the second STSL parameter, the bound. Theorem 6.22 supplies the best general explicit bound quoted in the paper, the surrounding text remarks that it grows like exp(c log(D(G_P)) D(G_P)^2), Example 6.23 gives a quadratic lower-bound construction for groups C_{n/2}⊕C_n, and Problem 6.24 then asks exactly for the rough order of magnitude of the bound in the STSL for L(G) in terms of D(G). The only substantive repairs needed are to make L(G)=L(B(G)) explicit, to use the paper’s natural choice Δ*(G), and to specify that 'smallest bound' means the optimal universal bound over all L∈L(G). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.08080))
